C.title: D. Reading comprehension
intro: A university library tested an automated tool that produced short answers to students’ research questions. In the first demonstration, the answers sounded confident and included detailed references. Some staff initially assumed that the presence of references made the answers dependable.

A later audit found that several references were inaccurate and two did not exist. Other answers were correct but omitted evidence that challenged the conclusion. The auditors argued that fluency and apparent precision were poor substitutes for checking sources and representing uncertainty. They did not conclude that the tool had no value; rather, they questioned the conditions under which its output should be trusted.

The library kept the tool for suggesting search terms and outlining possible questions. However, it required students to open original sources, verify quotations and distinguish a source’s findings from their own interpretations. Staff also recorded the tool’s recurring errors so that future evaluations could assess reliability across different subjects instead of relying on a persuasive demonstration.

questions.question: What initially encouraged some staff to trust the answers?
What did the audit discover?
options: The tool could not produce fluent language
Some references were inaccurate or nonexistent

questions.question: What did the auditors question?
options: The conditions under which the output could be trusted
Whether students should ever ask questions

questions.question: Why did the library record recurring errors?
options: To assess reliability across different subjects

questions.question: Which principle best reflects the library’s final approach?
options: Use the tool selectively and verify its output

E.title: E. Paragraph writing
intro: Write a reasoned paragraph responding to this claim: “Convenient information is not always reliable information.” State your position, discuss a counterargument, and explain how a learner or professional can make a responsible decision. Use precise language and examples. Aim for 150–180 words.
